newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila may be in market for U.S. corn, wheat.
newsitem.headline: Manila may be in market for U.S. corn, wheat.

text.p: Philippine firms are expected to shop for more U.S. corn and wheat in the coming week to meet their short-term requirements, Manila grain traders said on Friday.
The state-owned National Food Authority (NFA) recently announced it may tender for 150,000 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn no 2 or its equivalent on October 29.
The NFA plans to sell the imported corn to local feed millers and poultry and hog farmers.
"We have advised traders that we are looking for U.S. yellow corn number 2, with shipments originating either from the U.S. Pacific Northwest, Gulf or Argentina," an NFA official told Reuters.
Philippine traders said they have been informed that the NFA wants the shipment to arrive by December.
But livestock farmers said 150,000 tonnes may not be enough to meet their requirements up to the first quarter of 1997.

Philippine Association of Hog Raisers president Soledad Agbayani told reporters late on Thursday that feed millers, hog and poultry raisers have asked the Agriculture Department to import another 250,000 tonnes of corn on top of the 150,000 tonnes.
This will help make up for shortfalls in local supply between the last quarter of this year and up to March 1997.
Since the start of the year, the Philippines has imported 250,000 tonnes of corn for animal feed from the United States and Argentina.

Traders said the prevailing price of yellow whole grain corn for feeds dropped to 7.0 pesos a kg from 7.20 pesos while the prevailing retail price of white whole grain corn used in making starch edged up to 7.30 pesos per kg from 7.20 pesos.
Philippine flour companies are also expected to come back into the market to buy more wheat if prices soften further, traders said.
Manila buys most of its wheat from Minneapolis, where the price of December spring wheat closed 2-3/4 U.S. cents down at $4.06-1/4 a bushel on Thursday.
On Friday, two firms told commodity houses that they were in the market for a total of 35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.

A day before that, a Philippine food manufacturer and flour miller bought 11,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat, 13.5 percent protein content, at $4.10 a bushel FOB Portland, and another 6,000 tonnes of western white wheat at $4.0 a bushel FOB from the same port, traders said.
The firm also bought 6,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans at over $200 per tonne FOB Portland for mid-November shipment.

Another Philippine miller also clinched a deal for 8,500 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat, 14 percent protein content, at $4.10 per bushel FOB Portland, and another 8,500 tonnes of western white wheat at $4.00 per bushel FOB from the same port.
The price did not include freight, traders said.

Traders said prevailing retail price of a 25 kg bag of hard flour in Metro Manila dropped to 290 pesos from last week's 300 pesos while the prevailing retail price of soft flour remained unchanged at 260 pesos.
